name: mouse

attributes.attribute: a small beast of British folk belief
one caught in a sieve, or that swam past a boat, told of death at sea
one that left a house told of death in that home

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The mouse is a small beast of British belief. It is far from sure that the Celts gave it magic power. A trace of such a belief stayed in the Cotswolds of England. There the folk said that a rat could see the fate to come. A rat that left a house was a sign of death in that home. A rat, or a mouse, caught in a sieve told of danger to all who took to the sea. Their ship would leak as many holes as the sieve had laid bare. In Scotland a mouse that swam past a boat told plainly that a crewman would die at sea. The small wall beast thus grew to be an omen of the death that it could read in the fate of men.

okr.objective: Document the mouse as an omen.
key_results: Record the mouse as a small beast of British belief.
Record the sign of the mouse in a sieve or by a boat.
Record the sign of the rat that left a house.
